value.body: A science degree that applies chemistry, biology and physics to crime evidence: crime-scene management, fingerprints, questioned documents, toxicology, serology and DNA basics, ballistics and digital evidence, along with criminal law basics and lab work. It leads to private forensic and investigation work, government forensic lab posts (usually after a master's), or an M.Sc.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 years for Honours / Honours with Research under the UGC four-year UG framework (NEP 2020)

items.note: Only programmes reported under this discipline; some B.Sc Forensic Science courses may be counted under Science

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in the science stream (Physics, Chemistry with Biology or Mathematics). Admission is through CUET-UG at some central universities, the National Forensic Sciences University's own entrance test, or Class 12 merit and university tests at private and state institutions.

value.title: At a glance
items: The course is offered mostly by private universities and a few specialised institutions.
Government forensic lab posts are limited and usually ask for a master's.
Private work includes forensic labs, document verification and insurance investigation.
Specialising (DNA, toxicology, documents, digital forensics) usually happens at the M.Sc stage.
